wordmark.purpose: Product name at the left of the bar from 1700px wide, 800 weight.

label.purpose: Every control, menu item, menu group label, message bubble, canvas note name and pedal name, 700 weight.

body.purpose: Camera alert band and the soft plum second column in menus, 500 weight.

shadows.name: sticker

shadows.name: sticker-tight

motion.name: beat-flash
motion.value: 90ms, scale 1.35 drum stickers, 1.08 lift for a robot that acts, no easing
motion.purpose: A drum sticker jumps when the playhead fires it; a robot lifts when it does something.

motion.name: beat-swell
motion.value: first half of each sixteenth step, line width 1.45x, no easing
motion.purpose: A sounding melody line swells on the beat, with a white sparkle glint at the playhead.

motion.name: menu
motion.purpose: Select and dropdown menus open and close without animation.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Flash and swell stop; the playhead keeps moving.

breakpoints.name: wordmark
breakpoints.note: Below this the wordmark is screen-reader only.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.note: Below this bar gaps tighten to 6px, control side padding to 12px, the tempo slider to 96px, and pentatonic scale names shorten. The bar is one row at 1440px and wider and two rows from about 1024 to 1366px.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.note: Below this the bar reorders (settings first, then Camera, then tools and actions) and a 390px phone shows five rows, accepted because the instrument is laptop-first. Stage gutters narrow to 34px and 42px.

focus.purpose: Global :focus-visible ring, outside cascade layers so it outranks component focus styles.

narrative.overview:
The screen is a bright photo sticker booth. You stand in front of the camera, your own picture fills the stage under a pink exposure, and everything you place on it is drawn with booth pen: a saturated colour core, a thick white cut edge, a soft plum drop shadow. The scribble is the instrument. A candy pink bar holds every control at the top; the rest of the viewport belongs to the grid.

The shell is quiet and the ink is loud. Chrome stays in two colours (candy pink and plum, with off-white sticker paper for light controls), so the saturated pens, stickers and robots on the stage carry all of the colour. Rank in the controls comes from weight, never from size or case. Motion is tied to the beat and stepped: things under the playhead jump to full size for a fraction of a beat and jump back, with no easing.

The world refuses the dark studio-plugin look: no knobs, meters, black panels or a piano-roll grid with one neon accent.
keyCharacteristics: Bright pink-lilac booth backdrop, plum ink for every word.
Booth pen treatment on everything placed: colour core, white edge, soft plum shadow.
A line's pen colour is its sound.
One rounded gothic face at one size, rank by weight.
Fully round controls on a single candy pink bar.
Registration ticks instead of ruled grid lines.
Beat-locked, stepped motion with no easing.

rules.name: The Two Colour Shell Rule
rules.body: Chrome uses only candy pink, plum and sticker paper. Saturated colour belongs to things on the stage. The one exception is a 14px round swatch in a control or menu item that names the stage ink it stands for (a sound's pen, a robot's tint).

rules.name: The Plum Only Rule
rules.body: All text is plum ink, soft plum for a secondary value, or sticker paper on plum. No grey text, no coloured text.

rules.name: The Ink Is The Sound Rule
rules.body: A melody line's colour comes from its sound, never from the order it was drawn in.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: Every piece of text is 15px. Rank comes from weight (500, 700, 800), from soft plum versus plum, and from plum fill versus paper fill, never from a larger size or uppercase.

rules.name: The Upright Rule
rules.body: No italic or oblique text anywhere, including canvas text. `font-synthesis: none` is set on the root so the browser never fakes a slant or a bold.

rules.name: The Edges Rule
rules.body: Controls live in the bar and the gutters. The grid itself carries no chrome; the pedal ring and its guides are instrument readouts that exist only while a pedal is pressed or held.

rules.name: The Stuck On Rule
rules.body: A shadow is always soft and plum, always falls straight down, and only marks something sitting over the stage. No hard offset shadows, no glow.

rules.name: The Cut Edge Rule
rules.body: Anything placed on the stage gets a white edge roughly as thick as its colour core (lines and the Singer ribbon: edge 2.1 times the core width; stickers: 0.62 of the radius; robot sprites: 8px; robot hand parts: 5px; the pedal ring: 12px under a 6px core). Without the edge it does not belong to this world.

dos: Do set every word at 15px in M PLUS Rounded 1c and rank it by weight (500, 700, 800).
Do keep chrome to candy pink, plum and sticker paper, and give the saturated pen, drum and robot inks to the stage; a swatch that names a stage ink is the only colour allowed in a control.
Do colour a melody line by its sound, and give any new robot kind an ink already in the pen or drum sets.
Do give anything placed on the stage a white cut edge and the soft plum sticker shadow.
Do keep robots under placed ink so the player's marks stay readable.
Do tell drums apart by sticker shape as well as colour.
Do step beat motion in a single jump with no easing, and remove it under reduced motion while keeping the playhead.

Do keep controls as full pills labelled in plain words, using the existing shadcn components, and put further settings in a dropdown menu with sentence case group labels and the current value in a soft plum second column.

Do keep UI text to the minimum: one sentence before the first play, one hint while the stage is nearly empty or the mouse plays a pedal, the pedal's name over its ring, and a short description per robot in the Robots menu.
donts: Don't use italic or oblique text anywhere, including canvas text, wordmarks and labels.
Don't put all-caps eyebrows, kickers or decorative labels above anything, including menu group labels.
Don't use JetBrains Mono (or any alias of it) anywhere, including fallback stacks.
Don't use em dashes in any copy, label or generated text.
Don't put an accent stripe on one side of a container, by border, pseudo-element, background or shadow.
Don't use gradient text, glass panels, glows or neon effects.
Don't add text sizes beyond 15px or uppercase labels to create hierarchy.
Don't draw ruled grid lines; mark intersections with registration ticks and dots. The pedal pad's dotted guides are the only full-length lines, and only while a pedal is down.
Don't drift toward the dark studio-plugin look: knobs, meters, black panels, a piano roll with one neon accent.
Don't add hard offset shadows; the only shadow is the soft, downward plum one.
